description.p: Postio is a local-first email client for IMAP, Gmail and JMAP accounts. Mail is stored on your machine in an encrypted store with its own full-text index, searched instantly offline, and read the way a native GNOME application should feel: fast, keyboard-first, and quiet about what it sends over the network. Several accounts share one unified inbox; every action lands locally first and reaches the server in the background, so it works the same offline.
Nothing leaves this machine that you did not ask for: remote images and read receipts stay off until you allow them, and there is no telemetry.

Postio Focus comes with it, a second launcher on the same mail: one dense inbox that calls out invitations, questions and to-dos, holds newsletters back into digests on a cadence you choose, and files spam and automated updates away, each with its reason.

description.p: Postio 0.4.2 is an alpha, and the first release since the local store was rebuilt. The mail client is the same one the maintainer reads mail in every day; what changed underneath is the engine, and what changed on top is a long list of things that used to wait.

ul.li: The store is Turso, a Rust rewrite of SQLite, with its own full-text index and page-level encryption. Your mail is stored the same way; what is gone is the vendored SQLCipher and OpenSSL build underneath it.

Search and navigation stay responsive while a large mailbox backfills: a keystroke takes priority over a sync pass for the store, and the full-text index of message bodies is built by its own task off the sync lane.
Message bodies are compressed per row and stamped with the parser that read them, so a body an older parser got wrong is fetched again on the next sync instead of staying wrong.
Messages whose quoted-printable encoding is not quite right are decoded leniently instead of showing "parts of this message could not be decoded".
Settled operations are pruned from the queue after thirty days and the store reclaims space when it is worth doing.
The macOS frontend over the same engine reads mail, searches and pages, and is built and tested but not yet released.
A WebKit process that dies is reported at once, in the app and in the test suite, instead of surfacing as a four-minute timeout.

A mailto: link from a browser or another application opens the composer with the address, subject and body filled in, including on a cold launch. The desktop entry had claimed the scheme since 0.1.0; the application had never handled it.

The 0.3.0 milestone is included in this release: several accounts with a unified inbox, OAuth 2 sign-in through the browser, and the Gmail and JMAP backends. Its tag was cut on 2026-09-11 but its release never published, so this is the first bundle that carries it.

There is no 0.4.0 or 0.4.1 bundle. Both tags were cut on 2026-09-19 and neither build reached the bundle — the release path had never once run to completion, and each attempt uncovered the next thing wrong with it. Nothing was ever published under either tag; 0.4.2 is the same contents, released.

description.p: The multiple-accounts and OAuth milestone. Its tag was cut on 2026-09-11, but the release workflow failed before publishing anything, so no bundle was ever shipped under this number; 0.4.0 is the first release that carries this work.

ul.li: Several accounts, each synced by its own engine, and a unified inbox that groups threads across accounts at read time.
Moving mail between accounts as a safe saga, and search scoped to one account with account:.
OAuth 2 sign-in through the system browser with PKCE; OAUTHBEARER and XOAUTH2 on IMAP and SMTP; automatic re-authentication when a refresh grant expires.
Gmail REST and JMAP backends behind the same MailBackend seam as IMAP.

description.p: One IMAP + SMTP account, fully usable offline after the first sync: inbox, folders and threads; read, archive, delete, flag and move; HTML and plaintext reading with attachments and quoted-message folding; compose, reply, reply-all, forward and drafts; local full-text search with an instant search box and operators; vim-style keyboard navigation, a command palette and configurable shortcuts; background sync and local undo.
